transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because I’ve been feeling low for a long time. I still get through my driving routes and my volunteer shifts, but most days there’s this heavy feeling on me. Like I’m just going through the motions, not really feeling like I’m fully in my own life.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About three years now. It started after my father died, and it’s just kind of stayed with me since then.
Have you ever experienced periods where your mood was unusually high, irritable, or you felt overly energetic, even for a short time?
No, I don’t think so. I can get annoyed sometimes, like anyone, but I haven’t had times where I felt unusually high or full of energy.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, or do you find that activities don’t bring you pleasure anymore?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I still do things when I need to, but I haven’t paid much attention to whether I’m enjoying them like I used to. It’s hard to say.
Have you noticed that activities you used to enjoy don’t bring you the same pleasure anymore, or that you’ve lost interest in them?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really thought about it that way. I still do my usual things, but I can’t say for sure if I enjoy them less or if I’m just kind of going through the motions.
Looking back, would you say that you’ve lost interest in things you used to enjoy, or that those activities don’t bring you the same pleasure anymore?
I guess I haven’t really noticed a big change. I still do the things I usually do, but I don’t know if I’d say they feel less enjoyable. I just haven’t paid close attention to it.
Would you say that most days, you feel down or low for most of the day, even if you’re still getting things done?

Yeah… most days, I’d say so. I still get through my routes and my volunteer shifts, but there’s this heavy, low feeling that’s kind of sitting on me a lot of the day. It feels like I’m just going through the motions more than really being in my own life.
Do you find that you feel tired or that you lack energy most of the time, even after resting or getting enough sleep?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I get tired sometimes, like anyone, especially after work, but I haven’t noticed feeling drained most of the time even after resting. I’d have to think about that more.
Do you find that you feel tired or lack energy most of the time, even after you’ve had enough rest or sleep?

I don’t think so, not most of the time. I get worn out after work or if it’s been a long day, but after I sleep or rest, I don’t usually notice that I’m still lacking energy. At least not in a way that really stands out.
Do you find yourself feeling worthless or guilty a lot of the time, even when things aren’t necessarily your fault?

Yeah, I do get that. I don’t know if I’d call it guilt exactly, but I compare myself to my dad a lot… the kind of man he was. Nobody’s really telling me I’m failing, but in my own head it feels like I should be further along, or handling things better than I am.
Do you find that you have trouble concentrating, making decisions, or staying focused on tasks, even when you’re trying to?

Yeah, a bit. I can still do my job, but I notice it more lately. Like I’ll be looking at delivery times and have to reread them, or I’ll stand there staring at the schedule board longer than I should. It’s like my mind just doesn’t lock onto things as quick as it used to.
Would you say that your low mood is present for most of the day, nearly every day, even if you’re still able to get things done?

Yeah… I’d say so. I still get my routes done and I show up for my volunteer shifts, but most days there’s this low, heavy feeling there. It’s like I’m moving through what I have to do, but I’m not really in it. Just kind of going through the motions.
Would you say that your trouble concentrating or making decisions happens most of the day, nearly every day, even when you’re not particularly stressed or tired?

Yeah, I notice it pretty often. I can still do my job, but lately I’ll catch myself rereading delivery times or just staring at the schedule board longer than I should. It’s like my mind doesn’t click into place as quick as it used to, even when I’m not especially worn out.
Would you say that you no longer take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in them, even when you still do them?

I’m not really sure I’d say that exactly. I still do the things I usually do, and I don’t know that I’ve completely lost interest in them. Some days they just feel more like routine than enjoyment, I guess.
Would you say that your low mood is present for most of the day, nearly every day, even if you're still able to get things done?

Yeah… like I said, it’s there most days. I can still get my routes done and make it to my volunteer shifts, but there’s this heavy, low feeling that kind of sits on me. I’m doing what I’m supposed to do, but a lot of the time it feels like I’m just going through the motions.
Would you say that activities you used to enjoy don’t bring you the same pleasure anymore, even if you still do them?

I’m not sure I’d put it that strongly. I still do those things, and sometimes they’re fine. Maybe they don’t always feel as enjoyable as they used to, but I haven’t really noticed it as a clear “no pleasure” kind of thing.
Would you say that you take less pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even if you still do them?

I don’t know… maybe a little sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed a big change. I still do the same things, and they’re not always exciting or anything, but I wouldn’t say I clearly take less pleasure in them.
Would you say that you take less pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even if you still do them?
I guess I’m not really sure. I still do the things I’ve always done, and sometimes they’re okay. I wouldn’t say I’ve clearly noticed that I enjoy them less… it’s just kind of hard for me to tell.
Would you say that you take less pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even if you still do them?

I think I’ve kind of answered that the best I can. I don’t really notice a clear drop in pleasure. Some things feel a little flat now and then, but I still do them, and they can still be okay. So I’m not sure I’d say yes to that.
Would you say that you take less pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even if you still do them?

Yeah, I don’t think I can say that for sure. I still do the same things, and sometimes they’re fine, sometimes just kind of routine. But I haven’t noticed a clear loss of pleasure, if that’s what you mean.
